<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{theorem:main}
 	The set of satisfiable \(\mathsf{SL}\) sentences is computably isomorphic to true second-order arithmetic. The same holds for the next-time Boolean-goal fragment of $\mathsf{SL}$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
A \emph{concurrent game structure (CGS)} is a tuple
	\(\mathcal G=\langle \mathrm{AP},\mathrm{Ag},\mathrm{Ac},\mathrm{St},\mathsf{tr},\mathsf{ap},s_0\rangle\)
	where \(\mathrm{AP}\) (atomic propositions) and \(\mathrm{Ag}\) (agents) are finite nonempty sets, \(\mathrm{Ac}\) (actions) and \(\mathrm{St}\) (states) are at most countable nonempty sets, \(s_0\in\mathrm{St}\) is the initial state, \(\mathsf{tr}:\mathrm{St}\times\mathrm{Ac}^{\mathrm{Ag}}\to\mathrm{St}\) is the transition function, and \(\mathsf{ap}:\mathrm{St}\to 2^{\mathrm{AP}}\) is the labeling function.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
An element \(\delta\in\mathrm{Ac}^{\mathrm{Ag}}\) is called a \emph{decision}.  A \emph{track} (\emph{path}) in $\mathcal G$ is a non-empty finite (infinite resp.) sequence
	\(
	\rho=t_0\ldots t_n
	\)
	(\(\rho = t_0 t_1 \ldots \) resp.)
	of states such that, for every $i<n$ ($i \in \mathbb N$ resp.), there exists a decision
	\(
	\delta_i\in\mathrm{Ac}^{\mathrm{Ag}}
	\)
	with
	\(
	\mathsf{tr}(t_i,\delta_i)=t_{i+1}.
	\)
	We write $\mathrm{Trk}_{\mathcal G}$ ($\mathrm{Pth}_{\mathcal G}$) for the set of all tracks (paths resp.) in $\mathcal G$. Moreover, for $s \in \mathrm{St}$, $\mathrm{Trk}_{\mathcal G}(s)$ ($\mathrm{Pth}_{\mathcal G}(s)$) denotes the set of all tracks (paths resp.) starting with $s$.
	
	If $\rho = t_0 t_1 \ldots$ is a path, then $\rho_{\le n} = t_0 \ldots t_n$.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
If $\rho = t_0 \ldots t_m$ and $\tau = t_m \ldots t_n$ are two tracks, then $\rho \star \tau = t_0 \ldots t_n$.
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
A \emph{strategy} is a partial function
	\(
	f:\mathrm{Trk}_{\mathcal G}\rightharpoonup \mathrm{Ac}
	\). \(\mathrm{Str}_{\mathcal G}\) denotes the set of all strategies. $f$ is $s$-total if $\mathrm{Trk}_{\mathcal G}(s) \subseteq \operatorname{dom}(f)$; the set of $s$-total strategies is denoted by $\mathrm{Str}_{\mathcal G}(s)$.
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
If \(f\in\mathrm{Str}_{\mathcal G}\) and \(\rho\in\mathrm{Trk}_{\mathcal G}\), define the \emph{shift} of \(f\) along \(\rho\) by
	\[
	f_{\rightarrow\rho}(\tau):=f(\rho \star \tau)
	\quad(\tau\in\mathrm{Trk}_{\mathcal G}).
	\]
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
The set $\operatorname{free}(\varphi)$ of free variables and agents of a formula $\varphi$ is defined inductively:
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{free}(p)&=\varnothing,
		&& p \in \mathrm{AP}, \\
		\operatorname{free}(\neg\varphi)&=\operatorname{free}(\varphi),\\
		\operatorname{free}(\varphi\circ\psi)&=\operatorname{free}(\varphi)\cup\operatorname{free}(\psi),
		&&\circ\in\{\land,\lor\},\\
		\operatorname{free}(\mathbf X\varphi)&=\mathrm{Ag}\cup\operatorname{free}(\varphi),\\
		\operatorname{free}(\varphi\circ\psi)&=\mathrm{Ag}\cup\operatorname{free}(\varphi)\cup\operatorname{free}(\psi),
		&&\circ\in\{\mathsf U,\mathsf R\},\\
		\operatorname{free}(Qx\,\varphi)&=\operatorname{free}(\varphi)\setminus\{x\},
		&&Qx\in\{\langle\!\langle x\rangle\!\rangle,[\![x]\!]\},
		\\
		\operatorname{free}((a,x)\varphi)&=
		\begin{cases}
			\operatorname{free}(\varphi),&a\notin\operatorname{free}(\varphi),\\
			(\operatorname{free}(\varphi)\setminus\{a\})\cup\{x\},&a\in\operatorname{free}(\varphi).
		\end{cases}
	\end{align*}
<!-- end definition-6 -->
<!-- definition-7: body_md -->
Given a CGS \(\mathcal G=\langle \mathrm{AP},\mathrm{Ag},\mathrm{Ac},\mathrm{St},\mathsf{tr},\mathsf{ap},s_0\rangle\), an \emph{assignment} is a partial map
	\(
	\chi:\mathrm{Var}\cup\mathrm{Ag}\rightharpoonup\mathrm{Str}_{\mathcal G}.
	\)
	For \(\ell\in\mathrm{Var}\cup\mathrm{Ag}\) and \(f\in\mathrm{Str}_{\mathcal G}\), the notation \(\chi[\ell\mapsto f]\) denotes the assignment with domain \(\operatorname{dom}(\chi)\cup\{\ell\}\) that maps \(\ell\) to \(f\) and agrees with \(\chi\) everywhere else. In particular, \(\chi[a\mapsto\chi(x)]\) assigns to agent \(a\) the strategy currently stored in \(x\). The assignment is \emph{complete} if every agent is in its domain: \(\operatorname{dom}(\chi) \supseteq \mathrm{Ag}\). The assignment is $s$-total if $\chi(\ell)$ is $s$-total for every $\ell \in \operatorname{dom}(\chi)$.
<!-- end definition-7 -->
<!-- definition-8: body_md -->
The \emph{shift} of an assignment $\chi$ along a track $\rho$ is the assignment $\chi_{\rightarrow\rho}$ with the same domain as $\chi$ such that $\chi_{\rightarrow\rho}(\ell) = (\chi(\ell))_{\rightarrow\rho}$ for each $\ell \in \operatorname{dom}(\chi)$.
<!-- end definition-8 -->
<!-- definition-9: body_md -->
Let \(s \in \mathrm{St}\) be a state and \(\chi\) a complete $s$-total assignment. A \emph{\((\chi,s)\)-play} is the path
	\(\operatorname{play}(\chi,s) = \pi = \pi_0 \pi_1 \pi_2\ldots\in\mathrm{Pth}_{\mathcal G}\) where \(\pi_0=s\) and \(\pi_{i+1}=\mathsf{tr}(\pi_i,\delta_i)\) for \(\delta_i(a)=\chi(a)(\pi_{\le i})\). 
	Define the \emph{global translation} of \((\chi,s)\) to position \(i \in \mathbb N \) by \((\chi,s)^i=(\chi_{\rightarrow\pi_{\le i}},\pi_i)\).
<!-- end definition-9 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:upper}
	\(\mathsf{SAT}(\mathsf{SL})\le_1\operatorname{Th}_2(\mathbb N)\).
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Every CGS has at most countable sets of states and actions, so its states, actions, transition function, labeling function, and initial state can be coded by subsets of \(\mathbb N\). (Note that the transition function $\mathsf{tr}: \mathrm{St} \times \mathrm{Ac}^{\mathrm{Ag}} \to \mathrm{St}$ maps a countable set to a countable set.) Tracks can be coded by natural numbers, therefore, a strategy \(f:\mathrm{Trk}\to\mathrm{Ac}\) is a second-order object. Once the strategies of all agents are fixed, every finite prefix of the induced play is arithmetically definable from the model and strategies.  \(\mathbf X\) and \(\mathsf{U}\) require only first-order quantification over positions of the play. Finally, the satisfiability statement is of the form ``there exists a CGS such that\dots'', so its coding requires an existential second-order quantifier. This allows one to transform a given $\mathsf{SL}$ formula $\vartheta$ into a second-order arithmetic sentence $\vartheta^\circledast$ whose truth in $\mathcal N$ is equivalent to satisfiability of $\vartheta$. The mapping $\vartheta \mapsto \vartheta^\circledast$ is clearly injective (each atomic formula and connective are translated homomorphically.)
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:injective-lower}
	$\operatorname{Th}_2(\mathbb N) \le_1 \mathsf{SAT}(\mathsf{SL_{\mathbf X}[BG]})$.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- definition-10: body_md -->
For a 5-tuple of strategy variables $\bar x=(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_b,x_c)$, put
	\[
	\mathsf B(\bar x)=(a_1,x_1)(a_2,x_2)(a_3,x_3)(b,x_b)(c,x_c).
	\]
	For $i\in\mathrm{Ag}$, the tuple $\bar x[i\leftarrow v]$ replaces the coordinate for agent $i$ by $v$. The quantifier block $[\![\bar x]\!]$ ($\langle\!\langle \bar x\rangle\!\rangle$) universally (existentially resp.) quantifies the five variables.
<!-- end definition-10 -->
<!-- definition-11: body_md -->
For each $i\in\{b,c\}$ define the closed sentences
	\begin{align}
		I_i &:= [\![\bar x]\!][\![\bar y]\!]
		\bigl(\mathsf B(\bar x)\mathbf X p_i
		\leftrightarrow
		\mathsf B(\bar y[i\leftarrow x_i])\mathbf X p_i\bigr),
		\label{eq-local-ind}
		\\
		P_i &:= (\langle\!\langle \bar x\rangle\!\rangle\mathsf B(\bar x)\mathbf X p_i)
		\wedge(\langle\!\langle \bar y\rangle\!\rangle\mathsf B(\bar y)\mathbf X\neg p_i).
		\label{eq-local-onto}
	\end{align}
	Let \(\mathsf{Test}:=I_b\wedge P_b\wedge I_c\wedge P_c\).
<!-- end definition-11 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem-local}
A state $s\in\mathrm{St}$ satisfies $\mathsf{Test}$ if and only if there are surjective functions
\(\beta_b^s,\beta_c^s:\mathrm{Ac}\to\{0,1\}\) such that, for every decision $\bar\alpha\in \mathrm{Ac}^5$ and $i\in\{b,c\}$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq-local-bit}
p_i\in\mathsf{ap}(\mathsf{tr}(s,\bar\alpha))
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\beta_i^s(\alpha_i)=1.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- definition-12: body_md -->
Define three closed sentences:
	\begin{align}
		L&:=[\![\bar x]\!]\mathsf B(\bar x)\mathbf X\mathsf{Test},\label{eq-all-local}\\
		J_b&:=[\![\bar x]\!][\![v]\!]
		\bigl(\mathsf B(\bar x)\mathbf X\mathbf X p_c
		\leftrightarrow\mathsf B(\bar x[b\leftarrow v])\mathbf X\mathbf X p_c\bigr),\label{eq-Jb}\\
		J_c&:=[\![\bar x]\!][\![v]\!]
		\bigl(\mathsf B(\bar x)\mathbf X\mathbf X p_b
		\leftrightarrow\mathsf B(\bar x[c\leftarrow v])\mathbf X\mathbf X p_b\bigr).\label{eq-Jc}
	\end{align}
	The variable $v$ is fresh in each formula. Finally set \(\mathsf{Good}:=L\wedge J_b\wedge J_c\).
<!-- end definition-12 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem-independence}
Suppose $\mathcal G,s_0\models\mathsf{Good}$. There is a function $q:\mathrm{Ac}^3\to\mathrm{St}$ such that
\\
\(
\mathsf{tr}(s_0,\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3,\alpha_b,\alpha_c)
=q(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3)
\)
for all decisions. Besides, every state in the image of $q$ satisfies $\mathsf{Test}$.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Fix actions $\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3,\alpha_c$ and two actions $u,v$ for $b$. Let
\[
s=\mathsf{tr}(s_0,\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3,u,\alpha_c),\qquad
t=\mathsf{tr}(s_0,\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3,v,\alpha_c).
\]
Suppose $s\ne t$. Since both $s$ and $t$ satisfy $\mathsf{Test}$, choose actions $\gamma_s,\gamma_t$ with
$\beta_c^s(\gamma_s)=0$ and $\beta_c^t(\gamma_t)=1$ (Lemma \ref{lem-local}). Define a single strategy $f_c$ by
\(f_c(s_0)=\alpha_c\), \(f_c(s_0s)=\gamma_s\), \(f_c(s_0t)=\gamma_t\). It can be extended arbitrarily to every other track. Choose some strategies $f_1,f_2,f_3$ such that $f_i(s_0) = \alpha_i$, and two strategies $f_b^1,f_b^2$ for $b$ such that $f_b^1(s_0) = u$, $f_b^2(s_0) = v$. 

If the strategies $(f_1,f_2,f_3,f_b^1,f_c)$ are played, the transition function takes $s_0$ to $s$ on the first move. Since $\mathcal G, s \models \mathsf{Test}$, it holds that $\mathcal G,(f_1,f_2,f_3,f_b^1,f_c)_{\rightarrow s_0s},s \models \mathbf X p_c$ iff $\beta^s_c(\gamma_s) = 1$---which is false. Hence, $\mathcal G,(f_1,f_2,f_3,f_b^1,f_c),s_0 \not\models \mathbf X \mathbf X p_c$.
Similarly, one can show that $\mathcal G,(f_1,f_2,f_3,f_b^2,f_c),s_0 \models \mathbf X \mathbf X p_c$, because $\beta^t_c(\gamma_t) = 1$.

Therefore, $\mathcal G, s_0 \not \models J_b$, i.e., the formula after the quantifier block is false when one assigns the strategies $(f_1,f_2,f_3,f_b^1,f_c)$ to $\bar x$ and $f_b^2$ to $v$. This is a contradiction. It gives us that $s=t$, so indeed the value $\mathsf{tr}(s_0,\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3,\alpha_b,\alpha_c)$ does not depend on $\alpha_b$. Symmetrically, one can show that it does not depend on $\alpha_c$, hence the desired function $q$ exists. Finally, the second statement of the lemma directly follows from the definition of $L$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- definition-13: body_md -->
\label{definition:d_f}
	For $f\in\mathrm{Str}_{\mathcal G}(s_0)$, let
	\(
	d_f:=q(f(s_0),\varepsilon(e)(s_0),\varepsilon(e)(s_0))\). Let 
	\[D:=\{d_f \mid f \in \mathrm{Str}_{\mathcal G}(s_0)\}.\]
<!-- end definition-13 -->
<!-- definition-14: body_md -->
Let
	\begin{align}
		\mathsf{Mem}(Y,x)&:=\mathsf B(x,e,e,Y,e)\mathbf X\mathbf X p_b,\label{eq-mem}\\
		\mathsf{Eq}(x,y)&:=[\![Y]\!]\bigl(\mathsf{Mem}(Y,x)\leftrightarrow\mathsf{Mem}(Y,y)\bigr).
		\label{eq-eq}
	\end{align}
<!-- end definition-14 -->
<!-- definition-15: body_md -->
For $F$ an $s_0$-total strategy, let \(\hat F:=\{d_f \in D \mid f \in \mathrm{Str}_{\mathcal G}(s_0) ~ \text{and} ~ \mathsf{Mem}(F,f)\}\).
<!-- end definition-15 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem-powerset}
If $\mathcal G,s_0\models\mathsf{Good}$, then $\mathcal P(D) = \{\hat F \mid F \in \mathrm{Str}_{\mathcal G}(s_0)\}$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Choose for each $d\in D$ actions $\gamma_d^0,\gamma_d^1$ with $\beta_b^d(\gamma_d^j)=j$. For any $U\subseteq D$, define a strategy $F_U$ as follows:
\[
F_U(s_0d)=\begin{cases}\gamma_d^1,&d\in U,\\\gamma_d^0,&d\notin U.\end{cases}
\]
For all other tracks, define $F_U$ arbitrarily. Then \(d \in \widehat{F_U}\) iff \(\beta_b^d(F_U(s_0d))=1\) iff \(d \in U\). Hence $U = \widehat{F_U}$, as required.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{corollary-eq}
	If $\mathcal G,s_0\models\mathsf{Good}$, then $\mathsf{Eq}(f,g) \Longleftrightarrow d_f=d_g$.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
\leavevmode
	
	$(\Longrightarrow)$ If $d_f\ne d_g$, let $U = \{d_f\}$. Then $\mathsf{Mem}(F_U,f)$ and $\neg\mathsf{Mem}(F_U,g)$ hold, therefore, \(\neg\mathsf{Eq}(f,g)\).
	
	$(\Longleftarrow)$ Follows from \eqref{eq-mem-sem}.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- definition-16: body_md -->
Let
	\begin{align}
		\mathsf{Succ}(x,y)&:=\mathsf B(x,y,e,e,e)\mathbf X p_S,\label{eq-succ}\\
		\mathsf{Add}(x,y,z)&:=\mathsf B(x,y,z,e,e)\mathbf X p_A,\label{eq-add}\\
		\mathsf{Mult}(x,y,z)&:=\mathsf B(x,y,z,e,e)\mathbf X p_M.\label{eq-mult}
	\end{align}
<!-- end definition-16 -->
<!-- definition-17: body_md -->
For $R\in\{\mathsf{Succ},\mathsf{Add},\mathsf{Mult}\}$ of arity $k\in\{2,3\}$ let
	\begin{equation*}
		\mathsf{Ext}_R:=[\![x_1]\!]\cdots[\![x_k]\!][\![y_1]\!]\cdots[\![y_k]\!]
		\left(\bigwedge_{j=1}^k\mathsf{Eq}(x_j,y_j)
		\rightarrow (R(x_1,\ldots,x_k)\leftrightarrow R(y_1,\ldots,y_k))\right).
	\end{equation*}
	Let $\mathsf{Ext}=\mathsf{Ext}_{\mathsf{Succ}}\wedge\mathsf{Ext}_{\mathsf{Add}}\wedge\mathsf{Ext}_{\mathsf{Mult}}$. Let $\mathsf{PA}_2$ be the conjunction of the following statements:
	\begin{align}
		&\forall x\exists y\ S(x,y),\label{eq-s-total}\\
		&\forall x\forall y\forall z\ (S(x,y)\wedge S(x,z)\to y=z),\label{eq-s-fun}\\
		&\forall x\forall y\forall z\ (S(x,z)\wedge S(y,z)\to x=y),\label{eq-s-inj}\\
		&\forall x\ \neg S(x,0),\label{eq-s-zero}\\
		&\forall U\left[\left(0\in U\wedge
		\forall x\forall y\,(x\in U\wedge S(x,y)\to y\in U)\right)
		\to\forall x\ x\in U\right],\label{eq-induction}\\
		&\forall x\forall y\exists z\ A(x,y,z),\label{eq-a-total}\\
		&\forall x\forall y\forall z\forall w\ (A(x,y,z)\wedge A(x,y,w)\to z=w),\label{eq-a-fun}\\
		&\forall x\ A(x,0,x),\label{eq-a-zero}\\
		&\forall x\forall y\forall y'\forall z\forall z'\
		(S(y,y')\wedge A(x,y,z)\wedge S(z,z')\to A(x,y',z')),\label{eq-a-rec}\\
		&\forall x\forall y\exists z\ M(x,y,z),\label{eq-m-total}\\
		&\forall x\forall y\forall z\forall w\ (M(x,y,z)\wedge M(x,y,w)\to z=w),\label{eq-m-fun}\\
		&\forall x\ M(x,0,0),\label{eq-m-zero}\\
		&\forall x\forall y\forall y'\forall z\forall w\
		(S(y,y')\wedge M(x,y,z)\wedge A(z,x,w)\to M(x,y',w)).\label{eq-m-rec}
	\end{align}
<!-- end definition-17 -->
<!-- definition-18: body_md -->
We define the translation $\dagger$ on the formulas of the two-sorted relational language of second-order arithmetic. Choose disjoint infinite families of strategy variables to represent the number variables and the set variables, neither containing $e$. Let \(x^\dagger=x\) for $x$ a first-order variable, \(0^\dagger=e\). On atomic formulas, set
	\begin{align*}
		(t=u)^\dagger&=\mathsf{Eq}(t^\dagger,u^\dagger),&
		(t\in Y)^\dagger&=\mathsf{Mem}(Y,t^\dagger),\\
		S(t,u)^\dagger&=\mathsf{Succ}(t^\dagger,u^\dagger),&
		A(t,u,v)^\dagger&=\mathsf{Add}(t^\dagger,u^\dagger,v^\dagger),\\
		M(t,u,v)^\dagger&=\mathsf{Mult}(t^\dagger,u^\dagger,v^\dagger).
	\end{align*}
	Quantifiers are translated as follows: \((\exists x\,\varphi)^\dagger = \langle\!\langle x\rangle\!\rangle\varphi^\dagger\), \((\exists Y\,\varphi)^\dagger = \langle\!\langle Y\rangle\!\rangle\varphi^\dagger\). For Boolean connectives, $\dagger$ is defined homomorphically. Universal quantifiers are translated by $(\forall x\,\varphi)^\dagger=[\![x]\!]\varphi^\dagger$ and $(\forall Y\,\varphi)^\dagger=[\![Y]\!]\varphi^\dagger$.
<!-- end definition-18 -->
<!-- definition-19: body_md -->
Assume $\mathcal G,\varepsilon,s_0\models\mathsf{Ext}$. Define $0^D=d_{\varepsilon(e)}$ and the relations on $D$ by
	\begin{align*}
		S^D(d_f,d_g)&\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\mathsf{Succ}(f,g),\\
		A^D(d_f,d_g,d_h)&\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\mathsf{Add}(f,g,h),\\
		M^D(d_f,d_g,d_h)&\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\mathsf{Mult}(f,g,h),
	\end{align*}
	for $f,g,h\in\mathrm{Str}_{\mathcal G}(s_0)$. Corollary \ref{corollary-eq} and $\mathsf{Ext}$ ensure that these relations do not depend on the chosen strategy representatives. Finally, define \(\mathcal D = (D,0^D,S^D,A^D,M^D)\).
<!-- end definition-19 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem-interpretation}
Assume $\mathcal G,s_0\models\mathsf{Good}$ and $\mathcal G,\varepsilon,s_0\models\mathsf{Ext}$. Let $\varphi$ be a second-order formula in the language $\mathsf{RelAr}$. Let $\eta:\{e\} \cup \operatorname{free}_1(\varphi) \cup \operatorname{free}_2(\varphi) \to \mathrm{Str}_{\mathcal G}(s_0)$ be a strategy assignment such that $\eta(e) = \varepsilon(e)$. Define $\nu_1(x) = d_{\eta(x)}$ for $x \in \operatorname{free}_1(\varphi)$ and $\nu_2(Y) = \widehat{\eta(Y)}$ for $Y \in \operatorname{free}_2(\varphi)$. Then
\(\mathcal D, \nu_1, \nu_2 \models \varphi
\Longleftrightarrow
\mathcal G,\eta,s_0\models\varphi^\dagger\).
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
The cases where $\varphi$ is atomic follow from Corollary~\ref{corollary-eq} and the definitions of the relation interpretations, using $\mathsf{Ext}$. Boolean cases are immediate. 

Let $\varphi=\exists x\,\psi$. If $\mathcal D,\nu_1,\nu_2\models\exists x\,\psi$, choose $d\in D$ such that $\mathcal D,\nu_1[x\mapsto d],\nu_2\models\psi$. By the definition of $D$, there is $f\in\mathrm{Str}_{\mathcal G}(s_0)$ with $d_f=d$. The assignment $\eta[x\mapsto f]$ corresponds precisely to $\nu_1[x\mapsto d]$ and $\nu_2$. By the induction hypothesis,
$\mathcal G,\eta[x\mapsto f],s_0\models\psi^\dagger$, hence
$\mathcal G,\eta,s_0\models\langle\!\langle x\rangle\!\rangle\psi^\dagger$. The converse is shown by reading these lines backwards.

Let $\varphi=\exists Y\,\psi$. If $\mathcal D,\nu_1,\nu_2\models\exists Y\,\psi$, choose $U\subseteq D$ such that $\mathcal D,\nu_1,\nu_2[Y\mapsto U]\models\psi$. Lemma~\ref{lem-powerset} gives $F\in\mathrm{Str}_{\mathcal G}(s_0)$ with $\hat F=U$. The assignment $\eta[Y\mapsto F]$ corresponds to $\nu_1$ and $\nu_2[Y\mapsto U]$. Therefore, the induction hypothesis yields
$\mathcal G,\eta[Y\mapsto F],s_0\models\psi^\dagger$, and thus
$\mathcal G,\eta,s_0\models\langle\!\langle Y\rangle\!\rangle\psi^\dagger$. Again, the converse is shown by reading the lines backwards.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lem-standard}
If $\mathcal D \models\mathsf{PA}_2$, then $\mathcal D$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal N$.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
By~\eqref{eq-s-total}--\eqref{eq-s-zero}, $S^D$ is the graph of an injective total function $s:D\to D$ such that $0^D$ is outside its range. The set \(
C := \{s^n(0^D) \mid n\in\mathbb N\}\subseteq D
\)
contains zero and is closed under $s$. Then,~\eqref{eq-induction} instantiated with $U = C$ yields that $C=D$. Thus the function $\iota:\mathbb N \to D$ defined by $\iota(n)=s^n(0^D)$ is surjective. If $\iota(m)=\iota(n)$ with $m<n$, injectivity of $s$ would give $0^D=s^{n-m}(0^D)$, contrary to~\eqref{eq-s-zero}. Hence $\iota$ is a bijection preserving zero and successor. The axioms \eqref{eq-a-total}--\eqref{eq-m-rec} guarantee that $A^D(\iota(m),\iota(n),\iota(k))$ is equivalent to $m+n=k$ (the proof is by induction on $n$) and, similarly, $M^D(\iota(m),\iota(n),\iota(k))$ is equivalent to $mn=k$.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- definition-20: body_md -->
For a closed second-order arithmetic sentence $\theta$, let
	\begin{equation}\label{eq-reduction}
		\Phi_\theta:=\mathsf{Good} \wedge \langle\!\langle e\rangle\!\rangle\bigl(\mathsf{Ext}\wedge\mathsf{PA}_2^\dagger \wedge\theta^\dagger\bigr).
	\end{equation}
<!-- end definition-20 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:lower}
For every closed sentence $\theta$ of second-order arithmetic,
\[
\mathcal N\models\theta
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Phi_\theta ~\text{is satisfiable}.
\]
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
\leavevmode

$(\Longleftarrow)$ Suppose $\mathcal G,s_0\models\Phi_\theta$. There is $\varepsilon : \{e\} \to \mathrm{Str}_{\mathcal G}(s_0)$ such that $\mathcal G,\varepsilon,s_0 \models \mathsf{Ext}\wedge\mathsf{PA}_2^\dagger \wedge\theta^\dagger$. Using $\mathcal G,\varepsilon,s_0$, define the structure $\mathcal D$ as above. Lemmas~\ref{lem-interpretation} and~\ref{lem-standard} show that it is isomorphic to $\mathcal N$. Lemma \ref{lem-interpretation} applied to $\theta^\dagger$ also gives that $\mathcal D \models \theta$, hence $\mathcal N \models \theta$.

$(\Longrightarrow)$ We define a CGS \(\mathcal G = \langle \mathrm{AP},\mathrm{Ag},\mathrm{Ac},\mathrm{St},\mathsf{tr},\mathsf{ap},s_0\rangle\) satisfying $\Phi_\theta$. Take $\mathrm{Ac}=\mathbb N$ and $\mathrm{St} = \{s_0\} \cup \{ t_{i,j,k} \mid i,j,k\in\mathbb N\} \cup \{ u_{\vartheta,\zeta} \mid \vartheta,\zeta\in\{0,1\}\}$. For a decision $(i,j,k,v,w)$ set
\begin{align*}
\mathsf{tr}(s_0,i,j,k,v,w)&=t_{i,j,k},\\
\mathsf{tr}(t_{i^\prime,j^\prime,k^\prime},i,j,k,v,w)&=u_{v\bmod2,w\bmod2},\\
\mathsf{tr}(u_{\vartheta,\zeta},i,j,k,v,w)&=u_{\vartheta,\zeta}.
\end{align*}
$\mathsf{ap}(t_{i,j,k})$ is the subset of $\{p_S,p_A,p_M\}$ such that
\[
p_S \in \mathsf{ap}(t_{i,j,k}) \iff j=i+1,\quad p_A \in \mathsf{ap}(t_{i,j,k}) \iff k=i+j,\quad p_M \in \mathsf{ap}(t_{i,j,k}) \iff k=ij.
\]
At $u_{\vartheta,\zeta}$, let $p_b$ hold exactly when $\vartheta=1$ and $p_c$ exactly when $\zeta=1$; no arithmetic proposition holds there. No propositions hold at $s_0$. This completes the definition of $\mathcal G$. Let us check that $\mathcal G,s_0 \models \Phi_\theta$.

\begin{itemize}
	\item The states reachable from $s_0$ in one move are exactly $t_{i,j,k}$. At such a state, the transition
	\[
	\mathsf{tr}(t_{i,j,k},i^\prime,j^\prime,k^\prime,v,w)=u_{v\bmod2,w\bmod2}
	\]
	depends only on $v,w$. At the resulting state, $p_b$ holds iff $v$ is odd, and $p_c$ holds iff $w$ is odd. Each agent can choose either parity independently. Thus $\mathcal G,t_{i,j,k}\models\mathsf{Test}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem-local}, and $\mathcal G,s_0\models L$.
	
	\item Let $(f_1,f_2,f_3,f_b,f_c)$ be an $s_0$-total strategy assignment and put $t=t_{f_1(s_0),f_2(s_0),f_3(s_0)}$. Then
	\begin{align*}
	&\mathcal G,(f_1,f_2,f_3,f_b,f_c),s_0\models\mathbf X\mathbf X p_c\\
	&\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
	\mathcal G,(f_1,f_2,f_3,f_b,f_c)_{\rightarrow s_0t},t\models\mathbf X p_c\\
	&\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
	\mathcal G,u_{f_b(s_0t)\bmod2,f_c(s_0t)\bmod2}\models p_c\\
	&\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f_c(s_0t)\bmod2=1.
	\end{align*}
	Consequently, the truth of \(\mathbf X \mathbf X p_c\) at $s_0$ does not depend on $b$'s strategy, so $J_b$ is true at $s_0$. Symmetrically, we can show that $\mathcal G,s_0 \models J_c$, hence $\mathcal G,s_0 \models \mathsf{Good}$.
	
	\item We need to show that there is a strategy assignment $\varepsilon:\{e\} \to \mathrm{Str}_{\mathcal G}(s_0)$ such that $\mathcal G, \varepsilon, s_0 \models \mathsf{Ext}\wedge\mathsf{PA}_2^\dagger \wedge\theta^\dagger$. Let $\varepsilon(e)$ be a constant-zero strategy (it outputs action $0$ on each input). In this case, $d_f=t_{f(s_0),0,0}$ for every $f \in \mathrm{Str}_{\mathcal G}(s_0)$. Therefore, $\mathsf{Eq}(f,g)$ holds iff $f(s_0) = g(s_0)$, hence $\mathsf{Eq}$ identifies strategies with their actions on the initial state. $\mathsf{Succ}(f,g)$ holds iff $\mathcal G,(f,g,\varepsilon(e),\varepsilon(e),\varepsilon(e)), s_0 \models \mathbf X p_S$ iff $p_S \in \mathsf{ap}(t_{f(s_0),g(s_0),0})$ iff $g(s_0) = f(s_0)+1$. Similarly, $\mathsf{Add}(f,g,h)$ holds iff $h(s_0) = f(s_0) + g(s_0)$ and $\mathsf{Mult}(f,g,h)$ holds iff $h(s_0) = f(s_0) g(s_0)$. This immediately yields that $\mathcal G, \varepsilon, s_0 \models \mathsf{Ext}\wedge\mathsf{PA}_2^\dagger$. 
	
	Define $\mathcal D$ from $\mathcal G,\varepsilon,s_0$ as before. Then, $\mathcal D$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal N$. By Lemma~\ref{lem-interpretation}, since $\mathcal N \models \theta$ and therefore $\mathcal D \models \theta$, $\mathcal G,\varepsilon,s_0 \models \theta^\dagger$. Thus, $\Phi_\theta$ is satisfiable in $\mathcal G,s_0$. \qedhere
\end{itemize}
<!-- end proof-7 -->
